Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the call this morning - great to learn more about Acme's unified product search use case and the latency/throughput constraints you mentioned. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: replace current on-prem ranking pipeline for search with an LLM-based reranker while keeping p95 latency under 250ms for peak traffic and preserving current relevance.
- Priority prompt set: short product titles + user intent (avg 12 tokens prompt, 32 tokens generation).
- Success metrics: MAP@10 >= current baseline, p95 latency < 250ms, cost per 1k queries <= your budget target.

Recommended immediate follow-ups I can own:
1) Share Redwood-verified benchmark links and a prompt set we used for a similar retailer.
2) Suggest 2 candidate model variants to start evals (one low-cost/fast, one higher quality).
3) Schedule a short technical benchmark review next week (30 min).

I've attached an initial prompt set and a one-page summary of the quick benchmark we ran against a sample of your dataset. Links & attachments below.

Recommended models (initial):
- redwood-3b-8k-quant (cost-optimized): typical throughput ~420 TPS on our N4 GPU profile; p50 latency ~28ms; p95 latency ~120ms. Good first pass for recall/fast reranking.
- redwood-7b-16k-quant (quality-focused): throughput ~220 TPS; p50 latency ~48ms; p95 latency ~210ms. Better for edge cases and complex product titles.

Attachments: [attachment: acme_prompt_set_v1.json (json)], [attachment: initial_benchmark_summary.pdf (pdf)]

Next steps: can you confirm the sample size you'd like us to run for a full eval, and whether procurement should be looped in now? I'm free Tuesday/Wednesday next week for the benchmark review.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Emma - thanks for the prompt questions and for looping procurement. Quick update after internal checks: 

- Quality regressions: we ran a rapid branded-query slice against redwood-3b-8k-quant and redwood-7b-16k-quant using your sample prompt set. For branded queries (n=1,200), redwood-3b showed a -3.2% delta in precision@1 vs your current ranker; redwood-7b showed a +0.6% improvement. The 3b tradeoff is latency/cost vs a small precision hit on very short branded terms.

- Performance profiles (Redwood-verified):
  * redwood-3b-8k-quant - throughput: 420 TPS (avg, N4 instance); p50 latency: 28ms; p95 latency: 120ms; cost: $0.09 / 1k queries (approx).
  * redwood-7b-16k-quant - throughput: 220 TPS; p50 latency: 48ms; p95 latency: 210ms; cost: $0.23 / 1k queries (approx).

I've published the full run results and a CSV export of per-query deltas to our benchmark dashboard and attached the CSV for your convenience. Links: 
- Redwood benchmark dashboard (run RDW-4821): https://redwooddash.local/benchmarks/RDW-4821
- Prompt set & prompt examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePromptSets
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/RDW-4821

Attachment: [attachment: 20260318-acme-benchmark-details.csv (csv)]

Recommended next steps: 
1) If minimizing cost is the primary driver, run a 2-week validation on redwood-3b with a small canary (5% traffic) and monitor precision@1 on branded queries. We can automatically fallback to the 7b variant for queries that trigger a low-confidence signal.
2) If you want parity/improvement on branded queries on day one, start with redwood-7b and we can tune prompts + response filtering to reduce tail regressions.

I'll schedule a 30-min benchmark review for Tuesday 3/23 at 10am PT - will send a calendar invite. For procurement, happy to share SOC2 artifacts via the secure portal; our security team will follow up on the attached questionnaire.

Let me know if you'd like any additional slices on the run. Happy to run a targeted eval for your branded-query list overnight.

Best,
Marissa
